Get the bag repaired and keep the receipt, since Wizz Air will cover the repair costs shown on it. If the bag is beyond repair, get a written confirmation from the repair shop stating its type and value. Then submit a claim under 'Bag damage' on the Wizz Air website, attaching the PIR copy and the repair receipt. If you only notice the damage after leaving the airport, report it at the airport within 7 days of arrival. Under the General Conditions, a written claim for damage must be made as soon as you discover it and at the latest within seven days of receiving the bag. Damage to unchecked baggage or personal property must be reported on board the aircraft. Minor exterior damage such as scratches, dents or staining is not covered.

questions.question: I'm flying to Spain for a cycling holiday. Can I take my own road bike (around 12 kg) and how should I pack it?

reply.text: Yes. Wizz Air lets you carry one piece of sports equipment, including a bicycle, for an additional fee, as long as it does not exceed 149 x 119 x 171 cm and 32 kg, so your 12 kg bike is within the weight limit. Add it during booking or in your WIZZ Profile at least 3 hours before departure, though booking is recommended because space per flight is limited. The General Conditions also say bicycles must be declared through the Call Centre at booking, and the fee is €55.00 to €65.00 online or by Call Centre, or €70.00 at the airport. To pack it, use a bicycle travel case with the wheels and pedals removed and the handlebars turned parallel, or cardboard with the tyres deflated. Wizz Air cannot supply packaging, so you must bring your own.
